findings.title: Every null is applied to A3 (and A2), so the evaluator marks A3 non-discriminating and E007 can never PASS
findings.detail: In the spec, null_baselines (die_position, stratum_mean, isolated_die) use applies_to = [A1, A2, A3, A4] (anchor &id001), so switch_spread_err_p95_K_max_load and tjavg_local_rel_err_p95_max_load are included. Under rules v2, mfos's evaluator (evaluate.py _annotate, lines 425-437) treats a pass criterion that any declared null also meets as 'non_discriminating', and that counts as not satisfied. O002 says the opposite should be tolerated: 'A3 (spread within 1 K) and A5 (speed) are each met by a layout-ignorant predictor on their own' (objective.yaml line 20), and 'A stratum-mean spread may meet A3 alone ... A4 carries the spread test' (A3 description). F2 requires the nulls to fail only A1, and the spread nulls to fail A4. The repository's own development data confirm the conflict. research/notes/o002-l1-design.md (null table) gives the stratum_mean and die_position nulls A3-type p95 of 0.411 K at P_ref and 0.193 K at half load, far under A3's 1.0 K. So A3 will be non_discriminating and the best possible E007 verdict is INCONCLUSIVE. The draft's own pre-registration gate (`mfos exp check E007 --rows <dev rows>` must show null discrimination, per founder_decisions_before_registration) would also fail on A3. The selftest never computes a null's A3 (it reports only A1, A2 and A4 per null), so it cannot catch this.
findings.evidence: E007.yaml null_baselines: applies_to &id001 lists dtj_pair_err_p95_K_max_load, tjavg_local_rel_err_p95_max_load, switch_spread_err_p95_K_max_load and switch_spread_err_ratio_vs_stratum_mean, reused by all three nulls. evaluate.py lines 26-29 and 431-436: 'a criterion that a null predictor also meets is non_discriminating and counts as not satisfied'. evaluate.py null_check, lines 440-462. o002-l1-design.md lines 88-91: stratum_mean and die_position A3-type 0.411 / 0.193 K. O002 objective.yaml lines 20 and 80.
findings.suggested_check: Limit applies_to to the criteria F2 requires the nulls to fail (A1 for all three nulls; A4 for the spread nulls), then run `mfos exp check E007 --rows` on dev rows to confirm that A3 and A2 are not flagged.

findings.title: The selftest never runs the real reference path; node-growth and baseplate-mean checks are fakes in selftest
findings.detail: --selftest runs every reference solve through _fake_field. The real thermal_fem child_solve, _bottom_mean, the energy/Picard/CG fields of the real ThermalResult, and child_calibrate on a real solver are never run. In the fake path tb_trapz_K is set equal to tb_flux_K by construction, so baseplate_mean_consistent passes trivially. node_count_growth is forced True when FAKE. I checked these by other means: by reading the code, every attribute and meta key child_solve reads exists in ThermalResult/meta (tj_mean, tj_max, energy_balance as |Q_out/Q_in - 1|, picard_residual, dofs, meta lines/q_in_W/q_out_W/cg_hit_maxiter/cg_max_iterations/amg_gs_sweeps), and units are consistent (nodes and lines both in m). Using FEM.estimate_dofs on 180 layouts (15 strata x 4 die sizes x 3), DOF growth per level is 7.31-7.67, inside the 6.8-9.2 band. My attempt to run one real level-0 calibration and one level-1 solve through the runner was refused by the session's permission policy, so the real path is still unexecuted by anyone.
findings.evidence: e007_run.py line 908: g_ok = ... if not FAKE else True. Line 1033: fake rec sets tb_trapz_K = Tc + P.sum()/(h*area). Selftest log: every reference job shows 70000/560000/4480000 fake DOF.
findings.suggested_check: Add to the selftest one real level-0 child_solve on a small development layout, asserting energy balance, |tb_trapz - tb_flux| <= 1e-6 K and DOF growth.

findings.title: Per-stratum A2 bound is likely infinite or at the maximum order statistic with 20 layouts
findings.detail: The per-stratum rule applies the V4 Woodruff bound to one stratum's rows (20 layout units, t(19) at one-sided 97 %, c ≈ 2.0). For a p95 over 4-12 dies per layout per load, the jackknife se of F(theta) is about 0.024 or more when the dies are independent, and larger when they are clustered. So q + c·se reaches about 1, and the upper bound becomes the maximum or +inf. The 'reported, not gated' per-stratum bounds will often carry no information. This is analytic reasoning only: my synthetic check was refused by the permission policy.
findings.evidence: e007_metrics.woodruff_bound returns +inf when q + c·se > 1. all_metrics computes per_stratum_A2 with metric_with_bound on 20-layout subsets.
findings.suggested_check: Report how many per-stratum A2 upper bounds are infinite on the T0398 dev rows, or report the point value only.

findings.title: Seed freshness check covers fewer streams than the spec claims
findings.detail: The sealed_seeds_fresh check compares only sample['sub_seeds'] (layout and F7 generator seeds) against the forbidden list. The spec says 'the sealed seed and every derived stream seed'. The die_size, timing_order, l2_subset and f7_strata stream seeds are not checked. Those seeds only drive selection RNGs, so leakage risk is negligible, but the check does not do what its description says.
findings.evidence: e007_run.py seed_checks: subs = set(sample['sub_seeds'].values()). build_sample records only layouts:* and f7:* in sub_seeds.
findings.suggested_check: Record every stream seed in sub_seeds, or narrow the description.

findings.title: A5 timing is described as 'before any reference solve', but the level-0 calibration solves run first
findings.detail: config.l1.timing and the l1_timing_single_thread detail say the L1 phase runs before any reference solve. In execute() the P_ref calibration reference solves (level 0) complete before the L1 phase, which needs P_ref. Timing is unaffected: no solve is running, and the calibration uses development layouts. The wording is still inaccurate.
findings.suggested_check: Reword to 'after P_ref calibration and before any judged reference solve'.

findings.title: Two joint-power figures for m = 20 in the spec
findings.detail: config.bound.statement cites a joint power of 0.898 (t3, m = 20). founder_decisions_before_registration cites 0.531 at m = 20 for the as-measured L1 (T0434). These are probably different scenarios (0.6 x threshold vs as-measured), but the spec does not say so next to the 0.898 figure, and m stays open.

independent_checks_performed: Ran every definition-of-done command: --selftest (0 failures), --verify-freeze (all OK), --plan (717 reference solves, 56.7 expected / 61.1 upper CPU-h), ruff (clean), thermal_fem hash prefix a216d5fe3209bcee (matches)

Recounted the plan's solves by hand: 600 judged + 45 calibration + 24 F7 + 48 subset (L0 + L2) = 717. Recomputed the option B VM hours (≈22.1 h of over-cap jobs + 0.5 h overhead = 22.6 h); matches --plan

Computed FEM.estimate_dofs at levels 0-2 for 180 layouts (15 strata x 4 die sizes x 3 layouts): DOF growth per level is 7.31-7.67, inside the node_count_growth band 8 ± 15 %. This check is bypassed under FAKE in the selftest

Read thermal_fem's ThermalResult, the meta construction and solve_layout's signature: every field child_solve reads exists; energy_balance is an absolute value; mesh/nodes/lines units are consistent; Q_out = h∫θ dA, so tb_flux equals the Q1 bottom mean exactly
Checked mfos.metrics.gci_step_floor: F1 level-1 error = |v1 - v2| + finest-level estimate, as O002 F1 requires; pair-difference hottest die fixed by level-1 argmax
Checked draw_die_size_mm: uniform(4.0, 5.5) snapped to the 0.5 mm grid gives weights (1/6, 1/3, 1/3, 1/6), matching the plan's weights
Checked the binomial order-statistic median interval for A5: indices (k-1, n-k) give X_(k), X_(n-k+1) with coverage ≥ 95 %

Traced the null path through mfos evaluate.py (null_values, _annotate, null_check) and compared spec applies_to with O002 F2 and the null A3 values from development data in research/notes/o002-l1-design.md (0.411 / 0.193 K, under A3's 1 K): blocker found
caveats: I could not run a real thermal_fem solve through the runner: the session's permission policy refused those commands (and a later synthetic bound simulation). So the real reference path, the baseplate-mean consistency on a real field, and the per-stratum bound behaviour are verified only by reading the code and by analysis.

The blocker assumes that registration sets ci on the recompute entries (as config.bound.recompute_ci_on_registration states), so the evaluator judges each null at its Woodruff upper bound. With ci: null, as in the draft today, the A1-A4 criteria would be 'missing' and the evaluation INVALID anyway.

The registration-time null_check would flag A3 before any compute is spent, so the defect costs a spec revision, not a wasted run. The draft as written still cannot pass its own stated pre-registration gate or reach PASS.
